explanation:
[EFFECT] Month has a non-monotonic effect on predicted hourly bike demand. January and February produce the strongest negative contributions (roughly −0.25 and −0.20 in log space), meaning demand is notably suppressed in the depths of winter. Contributions climb through spring and summer — hovering near or just above zero — then reach their highest point in October (around +0.35), before easing off in November and December. The pattern therefore dips in mid-winter, stays moderate across summer, and peaks sharply in autumn.

[IMPORTANCE] Month is the 4th most important feature out of 9, with an importance score of 0.086. It has a meaningful but not dominant influence on demand, sitting behind the top three predictors (likely hour, temperature, and year).

[RECOMMENDATION] Plan for significantly reduced bike availability and staffing needs in January and February, and prepare for the highest seasonal demand in October — ensuring maximum fleet readiness and maintenance coverage heading into autumn.
